findings.title: Access-token ID matcher rejects valid grant shortcuts
findings.body: `isAccessTokenId` compares the wrong substring and inverts the result. For a valid ID such as `onrtac:<uuid>`, `substring(3, 5)` is `ta`, not the grant shortcut `ac` at positions 4-6, so the authorization-code expectation returns false. Conversely, an ID whose incorrectly selected characters happen to match the expected shortcut is rejected. This causes the updated event assertions to fail for valid tokens (or accept invalid ones), so they do not validate the new format.

findings.title: Decoder cannot handle shortcuts permitted by the grant-factory contract
findings.body: The decoder hard-requires the encoded context to be exactly six characters, which means every grant shortcut must be exactly two characters. `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` neither enforces that requirement nor documents it (its new Javadoc even says shortcuts are usually three letters). A custom grant provider returning a three-character shortcut can issue an access token successfully, but attempting to decode its token ID always throws `IllegalArgumentException`. Validate and reject non-two-character shortcuts during factory initialization, or make the encoding self-delimiting/length-aware and document the supported format.

findings.title: Public Context copy constructor was removed without replacement
findings.body: This change removes the public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` constructor. Grant-type implementations in other modules/providers can use that constructor to preserve the request context while deriving a context, and will now fail to compile (or fail with `NoSuchMethodError` if compiled against the prior version). The added `grantType` field does not require removing the constructor; retain it and copy the new field to avoid this SPI compatibility break.

findings.title: Constructor does not validate raw token ID
findings.body: The fourth null check mistakenly validates `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. As a result, callers can construct an `AccessTokenContext` with a null raw ID despite the error message and apparent contract; encoding then produces an ID ending in the literal string `null` rather than failing fast. Check `rawTokenId` in this call.
